summary: Intermittent streaming disconnects behind corporate proxy; tool-call arguments occasionally incomplete (JSON parse errors)
environment: prod / us-east (customer traffic via corporate outbound proxy + WAF)
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports intermittent disconnects during SSE streaming responses when using Redwood Hosted API through a corporate outbound proxy/WAF. When disconnect occurs mid-tool-call, they sometimes end up with incomplete tool arguments (partial JSON) and their client attempts to parse/execute the tool call, causing downstream failures.

Impact
- End-user visible failures in their app (~0.5–2% of streamed requests per their logs; bursty)
- Tool calling flows more affected than plain text streaming due to partial arguments / JSON parse errors
- Customer currently retries full request, but is concerned about duplicate tool execution

Customer context
- HelioDesk, Inc. (enterprise) using Hosted API, TypeScript client
- Workload: chat completions w/ tool calling (1–3 tools) + streaming enabled; tool args can be 2–10KB JSON

Environment
- Region: us-east
- Client runtime: Node 20 (server-side)
- Network: corporate outbound proxy (TLS interception disabled per customer), WAF in front of their egress
- Timeouts: default node-fetch/undici timeouts (customer unsure) + proxy idle timeout suspected

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Send streaming request with tools enabled; ask model to call a tool with a larger JSON argument payload (e.g., complex search filters).
2) Occasionally the stream ends abruptly (no final event / no graceful termination).
3) Client receives a tool call with arguments that are not complete JSON (e.g., missing closing braces).
4) Customer code attempts JSON.parse on every tool-call delta and throws.

Observed behavior
- Stream terminates mid-response with client-side errors like:
  - "TypeError: terminated" (undici)
  - "socket hang up" / ECONNRESET
  - Occasionally: "unexpected end of JSON input" while parsing tool arguments

Expected behavior
- Stream should reliably deliver a terminal event indicating completion OR an error event, and customers should only attempt to parse tool arguments once the gateway indicates they are complete.

Customer-provided log snippets (sanitized)
Request headers (sanitized)
- user-agent: heliodesk-api/1.14 (node)
- accept: text/event-stream

SSE events (last few before disconnect)
- event: response.output_text.delta  data: {"delta":"I can look that up. Calling tool..."}
- event: response.tool_call.delta    data: {"tool_call_id":"call_01H...","name":"search_tickets","arguments_delta":"{\"project\":\"SUP\",\"status\":\"open\","}
- event: response.tool_call.delta    data: {"tool_call_id":"call_01H...","arguments_delta":"\"assignee\":\"owen\""}
- (connection closed; no final event observed)

Current customer implementation notes
- They treat each tool_call.delta as parseable JSON and attempt to parse/validate immediately.
- They do not gate tool execution on a completion marker.
- They do not apply an explicit per-request read timeout; rely on proxy defaults.

Initial hypothesis
- Corporate proxy/WAF buffering or idle timeouts causing stream termination.
- Customer-side parsing strategy for tool calls is unsafe: tool call arguments are streamed as deltas and may not be valid JSON until completed.

Requested outcome
- Confirm recommended client-side pattern for accumulating tool-call arguments across deltas and only parsing when complete.
- Provide mitigation steps for corporate proxies/WAFs (timeouts, buffering).
- If possible: confirm whether Redwood gateway emits a reliable end-of-stream event for tool calls; clarify semantics in docs.

Workaround / mitigation proposed (pending)
- Accumulate tool_call.arguments as a string buffer keyed by tool_call_id; parse only when the stream indicates the tool call is complete ("*.done" / final response object).
- Add client-side abort/read timeout > proxy idle timeout; ensure keep-alive settings.
- If behind NGINX: disable proxy buffering for SSE and increase proxy_read_timeout.

Attachments
- Customer HAR equivalent not provided (SSE); logs pasted above.
- Correlation IDs: rwreq_8b31d0c1..., rwreq_8b31d2a4... (provided via email to Support).
comments: 2026-02-06 10:14 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Created ticket after escalation from CS. Customer reports increasing failures this week. Asked for region, runtime, proxy/WAF details, and any correlation IDs.

2026-02-06 11:02 PT — HelioDesk (Customer) — Confirmed us-east, Node 20, outbound proxy (Zscaler) + WAF policy. Provided sample SSE transcript showing tool_call deltas and stream terminating without final message. Also shared they parse JSON on each delta.

2026-02-06 11:25 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Acknowledged. Explained that tool call arguments may arrive as partial JSON chunks. Recommended buffering by tool_call_id and parsing only once the tool call is complete. Requested their current parsing snippet to confirm.

2026-02-06 12:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Shared preliminary mitigation guidance for proxies:
- Ensure SSE is not buffered by proxy/WAF (disable buffering)
- Increase idle/read timeout for long-lived connections (>= 120s recommended)
- Prefer direct egress to Redwood endpoints where possible
Also suggested adding explicit request timeout handling with AbortController and retrying only when safe.

2026-02-07 09:03 PT — Dana Lo (TS SDK) — Confirmed expected semantics: tool call arguments are streamed as deltas; not guaranteed to be valid JSON until tool call is finalized. In TS examples, we now aggregate arguments and parse only after receiving the final tool call object / done marker. Noted this is a common pitfall and being addressed in docs refresh.

2026-02-07 10:41 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Provided customer with updated recommended pattern:
- Maintain map tool_call_id -> { name, argumentsBuffer }
- On each tool_call.delta: append arguments_delta
- Only JSON.parse(argumentsBuffer) after tool call completion (done event OR final response)
- If stream disconnect occurs before completion: do NOT execute tool; treat as retryable request.
Also added note: tool execution should be allowlisted/validated; never execute arbitrary tool names or shell/network calls from model output.

2026-02-07 13:22 PT — HelioDesk (Customer) — Implemented buffering + parse-on-done. Parse errors dropped to near-zero, but still seeing occasional disconnects (~0.7%). Asked for recommended timeout values and whether Redwood supports resuming streams.

2026-02-08 09:18 PT — Allison Grant (Reliability) — Pulled gateway metrics for the provided correlation IDs. Most disconnects show client-side close / upstream reset; no clear server-side 5xx spike. Recommended documenting proxy buffering/timeouts + adding metrics surfaced in upcoming gateway change (disconnect reason counters).

2026-02-08 10:02 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Responded to customer:
- We do not currently support stream resume from a mid-stream offset; treat disconnect as retry of the request.
- For tool calling, ensure retries are idempotent: either implement a request-level idempotency key on your side, or make tool execution idempotent (e.g., dedupe by request ID).
- Suggested: set overall request deadline 2–5 minutes, and ensure proxy idle timeout exceeds expected generation time; enable keep-alive; disable proxy buffering for SSE.
Linked internal troubleshooting write-up that will be published to docs shortly.

2026-02-09 14:36 PT — HelioDesk (Customer) — After proxy config change (disable buffering, increased idle timeout to 180s), disconnect rate improved significantly (<0.1% so far). Requested confirmation they are handling tool args correctly; shared snippet for review.

2026-02-09 15:10 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Reviewed snippet and confirmed correct approach. Noted one tweak: ensure you do not attempt to parse partial tool args when receiving name/id; only when completion event/final response. Suggested logging tool_call_id and a truncated argument preview (first 200 chars) for debugging, with redaction of sensitive fields.

2026-02-12 09:30 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Resolution: customer-side parsing fixed (aggregate deltas, parse on completion) + proxy/WAF config updated (no buffering, increased idle/read timeouts) resolved primary impact. Added references for upcoming docs updates and snippet patterns.
Follow-ups:
- Linked ENG-2850 to ensure troubleshooting section explicitly calls out proxy buffering + partial tool args.
- Linked ENG-2848 for gateway semantics wording alignment.
Closing as Resolved; will reopen if disconnect rate regresses.
resolution: Customer implemented tool-call argument aggregation and only parses/executes tools on completion; corporate proxy/WAF configuration updated (disable buffering, increase idle/read timeouts). Disconnect rate and tool-args parse failures reduced to acceptable levels. Docs/troubleshooting guidance linked for long-term prevention.
customer_facing_next_steps: Keep proxy/WAF SSE settings (no buffering, idle/read timeout >= 180s) and retain parse-on-completion tool call handling. If disconnects recur, provide new correlation IDs and timestamps for investigation; avoid executing tools after a truncated stream and treat as retryable with idempotency safeguards.
